result.title: Dynamic K-Head: Difficulty-Supervised Budget Selection for Continuous Latent Reasoning
result.summary: Chain-of-thought (CoT) improves reasoning but incurs substantial autoregressive rationale cost. Continuous CoT moves intermediate computation into recurrent hidden states, yet typically uses a fixed number of updates even though the best budget varies across questions and accuracy need not improve monotonically with $K$. We introduce Dynamic K-Head, a question-conditioned, pre-rollout budget selector. It is jointly trained with the reasoner under selected budgets, using difficulty supervision based on scores assigned from the question alone. We also show that latent-update count can misrepresent end-to-end cost because a short latent rollout can shift computation into a longer explicit continuation. We therefore count latent updates, implementation-specific special tokens, and all decoded text. Instantiated with CoDI on Llama 3.2 1B and GSM8K, Dynamic K-Head reaches 54.44% exact-match accuracy at 12.03 average reasoning/output tokens, compared with 52.31% at 15.21 tokens for fixed-$K=6$ CoDI---a 2.12-point gain with 20.9% lower token cost. Across three out-of-distribution arithmetic datasets, it reduces cost by 19.3--25.7% while improving accuracy by 0.30--2.22 points. These results demonstrate that difficulty-supervised budget selection can improve both accuracy and efficiency, while stable budget selection remains a central challenge.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 Dynamic K-Head：在连续 latent 推理中按问题难度、于 rollout 前预测 latent 更新次数 K，并与 reasoner 联合训练；同时在 CoDI+Llama 3.2 1B 上指出仅计 latent 更新数会低估端到端成本，主张统一核算 latent 更新、特殊 token 与解码文本。
AI.relevance_reason: 直接对应 LVR 中动态计算与停止决策（K 的选择）及推理成本度量，其「预算与准确率非单调」观察可供核查 latent 步数收益的边界。
